note: Task brief item 4 (game.js:560-627,676-696 DOM keyboard/mouse/pointer-lock listeners): a prior pass judged these 'no Unity analogue' without filing an exclusion. Re-checked line by line. VERDICT IS MIXED, not a blanket exclusion -- see the GameLoop.cs entry above for the two REAL behaviours this pass ported (pointer lock via Cursor.lockState, window-blur safety via OnApplicationFocus) because they were genuinely missing, not superseded. The lines below are the genuinely DOM-only remainder with no behaviour left to port, now that the real ones are out of this bucket.

proposed_excluded.what: the DOM event REGISTRATION calls themselves (not the handler bodies, which are ported separately or are Combat/HeldWeapon.cs's territory): the 3 window.addEventListener('keydown'/'keyup'/'blur', ...) calls, the 5 canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown'/'pointermove'/'pointerup'/'contextmenu'/'pointercancel', ...) calls, and `this.keys.delete(e.code)` (a hand-rolled pressed-key Set the JS needs because the DOM gives it nothing better)
proposed_excluded.reason: Unity's Input System polls Keyboard.current/Mouse.current directly every frame (already how ReadDiscreteKeys/HeldWeapon.Tick/TickOnFootCamera work in this port) -- there is no callback to register and no need for a parallel 'which keys are down' Set, Keyboard.current already IS that set. OnApplicationFocus (used by this pass for the _onBlur behaviour) is an engine-delivered lifecycle callback, not a registered listener, so it is not billed here either -- it is billed under its own behaviour in the GameLoop.cs entry above.

proposed_excluded.what: _onContextMenu (suppresses the browser's native right-click context menu while a weapon is drawn) and canvas.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId) (ties subsequent pointer events to the canvas element regardless of where the cursor wanders)
proposed_excluded.reason: Both are browser/DOM-specific affordances with nothing to replace: Unity has no OS context menu over the game view to suppress, and the Input System already reports global pointer state regardless of which element nominally 'captured' it -- TickOnFootCamera already reads Mouse.current.delta every frame with no capture concept at all.

note: Task brief item 2: devmode.js's manifest claim is 357/357 (100%, clamped down from an over-count of 406 -- see docs/port_units/README.md's own clamp log). That 100% is TRUE OF THE LEDGER but misleading about the FILE: read devmode.js end to end against Assets/Scripts/Tools/DevPlacementTag.cs + Assets/Editor/DevPlacement.cs. The persistence/registry/snippet half (register/_commit/reset/_store/world/snippet/copy/snapshot/apply, ~88 of 357 lines) is a real, functioning, probe-adjacent port (DevPlacement.cs's own header documents it in detail: EditorPrefs persistence, 3 redundant re-apply hooks, epsilon-guarded auto-commit polling). The REMAINING ~195 lines are the in-game TransformControls gizmo + its HTML/CSS panel, which DevPlacement.cs's own header explicitly calls out as A DELIBERATE SUPERSESSION ('the project decided Unity's own Scene-view Move/Rotate/Scale tools replace devmode.js's TransformControls overlay outright ... a second in-game gizmo would be redundant') rather than an oversight -- a reasonable, well-documented engineering call. The gap is bookkeeping, not behaviour: nothing in docs/port_manifest.json's `excluded` array reflects this, so the ledger currently reads '100% done' for a file that is really '~25% literally ported, ~55% deliberately superseded, 0% genuinely missing'. NOT filed as a real exclusion by this pass -- docs/port_manifest.json is the shared file every live agent folds into, and editing its `excluded` array directly (the only place merge_port_units.py actually reads exclusions from -- per-agent unit files only carry `covers` claims, confirmed by grep) is a write-conflict risk with 5 agents live. Proposing it here instead, for whoever next safely touches the manifest. Promoting this would lower devmode.js's OWN ratio not at all (100% in, 100% out, since the clamp re-tracks the shrunken budget) but would lower the overall core percentage slightly (~0.2pp) by removing a module that was inflating the average at an artificial 100% -- a more honest number, not a worse one.

proposed_excluded.what: the in-game gizmo + panel: hot getter, toggle/open/close/_ensure (TransformControls construction + the ` hotkey activation), select/deselect/cycle/_itemOf/_pick (click-to-select raycast), handleKey (Escape/bracket cycling), setMode/setSnap/toggleSpace (gizmo mode/snap/space buttons), _buildPanel/_render (the #dev-panel HTML/CSS + button wiring), _renderValues (live local/world/rot/scale text readout), dispose (gizmo/panel teardown)
proposed_excluded.reason: DevPlacement.cs's own header documents this exact supersession by name: Unity's native Scene-view Move/Rotate/Scale gizmo (the editor IS the gizmo) replaces the TransformControls overlay, and Unity's own Inspector already live-displays a selected Transform's local TRS, replacing _renderValues' hand-drawn text. DevPlacementWindow (the one new UI this port adds) covers the list/select/snippet portion of the old panel in a different, Unity-native shape (an EditorWindow, not an HTML panel) -- its own existence is why this is a supersession and not a silent drop.
